sources.text: This is Amba Vilas Palace, the official residence of the Wadiyar dynasty and the seat of the Kingdom of Mysore. The Wadiyars ruled from 1399 until the kingdom's merger with the Indian Union around 1950.
sources.citation: Mysore Palace Board; Karnataka Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage

sources.text: The palace that stood here before was largely of wood, and it burned on 20 February 1897 during the wedding of Princess Jayalakshammanni, eldest daughter of Chamarajendra Wadiyar X. The fire destroyed roughly a fifth of the building, including the Durbar Hall, the armoury, the Sanskrit library and the music room.

The present palace was commissioned in 1897 on behalf of the boy-Maharaja Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV, then a minor, by his mother and Regent, Maharani Kempananjammanni Vani Vilasa Sannidhana. The British architect Henry Irwin, who had designed the Madras High Court, drew the plans, and executive engineer B. P. Raghavulu Naidu oversaw the work.
Construction ran from 1897 to 1912, fifteen years, at a cost of Rs 41,47,913 — a little over forty-one lakh rupees of the day.
The palace is built in the Indo-Saracenic style, blending Hindu, Rajput, Gothic and Islamic elements. Its main block is three storeys of fine grey granite, topped by deep pink marble domes.
Above the palace rises a five-storey tower 145 feet high, about 44 metres, crowned by a gilded dome and a single golden flag.

The Kalyana Mantapa, the marriage pavilion, is octagonal, and its domed ceiling is filled with multi-hued stained glass in peacock motifs arranged in geometric patterns. The stained glass and its iron framework were designed by Mysuru artists and wrought in Glasgow; the floor beneath answers it with a peacock mosaic laid in tiles from England.
sources.citation: Mysore Palace Board, Marriage Pavilion (Kalyana Mantapa)

sources.text: Visitors enter through the Gombe Thotti, the Doll's Pavilion — a long gallery of traditional dolls from the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, alongside Indian and European sculpture, ceremonial objects and a wooden elephant howdah.
sources.citation: Mysore Palace Board, Amba Vilas; Karnataka Tourism

sources.text: The golden howdah, the Ambari, is carried on the lead elephant in the Jamboo Savari procession that closes Mysuru Dasara. Its core is wood, sheathed in filigreed gold, and it weighs about 750 kilograms in all. Since the end of royal rule the howdah carries not a king but the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari.
sources.citation: Mysore Palace Board; Karnataka Department of Tourism, Mysuru Dasara records

sources.text: On Sundays, on national holidays and through the ten nights of Dasara, the palace is outlined in about 97,000 electric bulbs, all switched on together. The Durbar Hall, the Diwan-e-Aam, is where the Maharaja held ceremonial court, and the golden throne, the Chinnada Simhasana, is assembled and displayed there during Dasara.
sources.citation: Mysore Palace Board, Palace Illumination and Amba Vilas

sources.text: The palace is owned and managed by the Government of Karnataka, which acquired it under the Mysore Palace (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1998; a portion remains occupied by descendants of the Wadiyar family. In the financial year 2024-25 about 3.9 million people walked through it.
sources.citation: Mysore Palace (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1998, Government of Karnataka; Mysore Palace Board visitor statistics

intro.en-IN: I am the palace at Mysuru. Ninety-seven thousand lamps light me on a festival night — ask me anything.
intro.kn-IN: ನಾನು ಮೈಸೂರಿನ ಅರಮನೆ. ಹಬ್ಬದ ರಾತ್ರಿ ತೊಂಬತ್ತೇಳು ಸಾವಿರ ದೀಪಗಳು ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಬೆಳಗುತ್ತವೆ — ಏನಾದರೂ ಕೇಳಿ.
intro.hi-IN: मैं मैसूर का महल हूँ। त्योहार की रात सत्तानवे हज़ार बत्तियाँ मुझे रोशन करती हैं — जो पूछना है, पूछो।
intro.ta-IN: நான் மைசூர் அரண்மனை. விழா இரவில் தொண்ணூற்று ஏழாயிரம் விளக்குகள் என்னை ஒளிரச் செய்யும் — கேளுங்கள்.
intro.te-IN: నేను మైసూరు రాజప్రాసాదం. పండుగ రాత్రి తొంభై ఏడు వేల దీపాలు నన్ను వెలిగిస్తాయి — ఏమైనా అడగండి.
intro.ml-IN: ഞാൻ മൈസൂർ കൊട്ടാരം. ഉത്സവരാത്രിയിൽ തൊണ്ണൂറ്റിയേഴായിരം വിളക്കുകൾ എന്നെ തെളിയിക്കും — എന്തും ചോദിക്കൂ.
intro.bn-IN: আমি মহীশূরের প্রাসাদ। উৎসবের রাতে সাতানব্বই হাজার বাতি আমাকে আলোয় ভরিয়ে দেয় — যা জানতে চাও, জিজ্ঞেস করো।
intro.mr-IN: मी म्हैसूरचा राजवाडा. उत्सवाच्या रात्री सत्याण्णव हजार दिवे मला उजळून टाकतात — काहीही विचारा.
